description:
f(n) when is_integer(n) and f(n :: integer) describe the same clause, but build different dispatch rows. The typed form becomes a row precondition (a type question the analysis reads, narrows the body by, and settles per activation: called with an int, the call is direct). The guarded form becomes an opaque Region::Guard: the analysis cannot read it (predicate_target returns None for guards), the body is not narrowed (probe: int|binary input, typed returns int|:other, guarded returns int|binary|:other), and the entry dispatch stays.

Design: page /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-sc8.49.html APPROVED 2026-10-31. Recognise, once, in guard_dispatch_from_rows (dispatch_matrix/pattern.rs:420): a helper whose two clauses are "annotated params -> true" and "plain params -> false" is a type predicate. Fold, once, in PatternDispatchProducer::add_row (pattern.rs ~680), which every row source passes through (entry, case, receive, lambda): top-level `and` conjuncts that call a type predicate with pattern-bound variables become type questions on those subjects; the rest stays the guard. Worked before fz-sc8.44, so trimming measures corrected plans.
title: A type-test guard is the same row as a typed parameter
